title: Simple Policy Gradients for Reasoning with Diffusion Language Models
claim: Prior methods use sequence-level likelihoods that are biased or intractable; ours optimizes individual denoising steps, so it is unbiased and tractable.
layout: 4 columns left-to-right, vertical dividers, checkmark comparison table beneath
description: The figure has four columns separated by vertical dividers. The leftmost column shows a dLLM generation trajectory from t=0 to t=m. Rows of five tokens go from all dark (masked) to all blue (unmasked). One token per step is highlighted orange, with small orange arrows pointing at it. The other three columns compare AR factorization, ELBO-based methods and AGRPO (ours). AR factorization has one long arrow from a blue sequence to an orange sequence, with a 'chain rule' brace beneath. ELBO-based methods randomly mask a sequence, then apply three arrows. AGRPO resamples a partially masked state at timestep t, with a single-token step and a 'repeat k times' brace. A table at the bottom has rows for Likelihood (Sequence, Sequence, Stepwise), Unbiased? and Tractable for dLLMs?, with ✓ and ✗ marks. The palette is blue, orange and dark gray.
caption: Existing RL post-training algorithms focus on sequence-level likelihoods and require either autoregressive factorization or ELBO-like bounds, which result in biased policy updates. Our proposed algorithm instead focuses on individual unmasking steps, aligning more naturally with the dLLM generation process.
abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) represent a promising alternative to autoregressive LLMs; however, the lack of effective post-training techniques, including reinforcement learning (RL), remains a key challenge for dLLMs, especially for downstream applications. Existing approaches often rely on a sequence-level view that requires biased likelihood approximations. In this work, we propose Amortized Group Relative Policy Optimization (AGRPO), a policy gradient algorithm that leverages the Markovian nature of dLLMs, optimizing individual denoising steps rather than full sequences. Our approach improves alignment between the trained policy and the inference process and also admits efficient, unbiased gradient updates via a novel timestep estimation scheme. We demonstrate AGRPO's effectiveness on different math and reasoning tasks, achieving absolute accuracy gains of +59.4\% and +69.7\% on Countdown and Sudoku over the base LLaDA model, exceeding comparable methods such as diffu-GRPO. Code is available at https://github.com/probablyabot/agrpo.
